lines.english: "…We're finished, right?"
"…Yeah."
"We're finished! We're finally finished, Haruki-kun!"
"Ah…"
"Look, it's just like I said, right? The two of us can do anything if we put our minds to it!"
"Ha, haha…"
It's 6 AM, and the sky is already beginning to grow bright.
On an early morning like this, when normally only the sound of the newspaper delivery bike can be heard,
…All we did was finish packing, though.
"Now we can leave everything else to the movers."
"They're coming in three hours, though."
Still, this was indeed an impressive feat.
Left with no more days off work until moving day, we were convinced that this would be a lost cause since Monday.
Then on Wednesday we were tied down all day at work, and on Thursday we were forced to participate in a hot pot party,
…I suppose that's the reason we're still awake at this hour.
"What now? Wanna sleep until the moving people arrive? Do you want breakfast? A bath? Or… me?"
"…Setsuna."
"Ah, I'm so sorry. Pretend you didn't hear that! I'm just in a weird mood right now."
"Haha…"
I guess I'm in a weird mood too, because I was just about to pick the last option without a second thought.
"But we probably shouldn't go to sleep right now… There's no way we'd wake up by nine."
"You're right."
Even now, I feel like I'm about to pass out unless I keep talking to her.
It feels like the fatigue of not just today, but the entire week is bearing down on me all at once.
At this rate, the two of us won't be able to enjoy the weekend at our new home.
If that happens, our first opportunity to unpack would be during the first three days of New Year's.
"So what do you want to do, really? Taking a bath or eating would be dangerous right now…"
"…Hey, Setsuna."
"Hm?"
"In that case, how about we go for a walk instead?"
"I'd love that!"
"Don't answer so quickly! Try to think and hesitate about it a little. I do happen to think I'm making a pretty weird suggestion right now."
Like I said earlier, we're both almost completely out of battery.
"No, it's okay… I'd have suggested the same thing if you hadn't first, Haruki-kun."
"Is that so…"
"Yup, it is."
But without a single hint of hesitation, Setsuna takes me up on my bizarre idea.
"So cold!"
"This is the coldest time of the year, after all."
During what is practically moments before New Year's, the icy cold wind dominates everything under the cloudless sky.
Little by little, brightness envelopes Minami-Suetsugu, and the sun can be seen poking its head as if to signal the beginning of a new day.
"Uuu, it's so cold, Haruki-kun."
"I know already."
Setsuna grabs hold of my hand without any hesitation.
Her hand isーas she herself puts itーlow in blood pressure, so it feels a decent bit colder than mine.
By the time our little walk is over, I'm sure it'll be the same temperature as mine.
Today… we will leave the apartment we have shared since university, and we'll move into a two-bedroom apartment five stations away.
And once we're there, our frequent visits to Minami-Suetsugu…
…Along with the scenery before our eyes, will all go away.
So let us ingrain it in our minds, so that we can always revisit it in our memories.
"Aah, I finally feel awake."
The morning sun shines from the end of the river, and its bright reflection bounces straight into our eyes.
The fatigue from my all-nighters combine with the fatigue from our walk, and the resulting adrenaline brings some energy back to my body.
"This place brings back a lot of memories, doesn't it?"
"…We only just started walking, you know?"
We're about ten minutes away from our apartment by foot.
And for Setsuna, this walkway is a path she went down nearly every day on her way to school.
"But we never use this path for commuting. It's opposite to Minami-Suetsugu."
"I guess you're right."
It may be close to where we live, but if we never visit it or have any use for it, we won't encounter it, and we won't think about it.
That's why looking for ourselves is important, to touch… Let's set aside what specifically I'm referring to.
"We walked this path together countless times during our school days."
"Yes."
It felt like a really long time, but in reality, it was only the last six months of high school.
In that short span of time, we walked side by side here countless times.
At first we'd awkwardly keep our distance, then we'd come closer together, and then finally, we'd hold hands like we're doing right now.
…And starting with our graduation, I began avoiding this path.
It didn't matter that we were in the same university, nor that her department's building was right next to mine.
"Once we move away, I wonder if this place will fill me with even more nostalgia than it does now."
"Don't exaggerate… This place is barely fifteen minutes away by train, and you could catch a taxi here for about 5000 yen."
"Jeez, why do you have to be so blunt? You don't have a hint of sentimental in you, do you?"
"You say that, but moving won't mean you'll visit your family any less often."
"You never know about things like that."
"But Setsuna, you love your family's place. Even now, you head over two or three times a month for dinner."
"When you put it that way, it sounds like I'm unable to let go of my parents."
"There's no need to let go."
"Well, I suppose you're right about that."
Like that, we ingrain the scenery of the riverside into the deepest recesses of our memories, talking about nothing in particular in the process.
The beautiful sight of the twinkling sunlight on the river surface. The satisfying cracking of ice when we step on it.
The endless memories I share with Setsuna here, and the memories of her absence.
"…By the way, Setsuna."
"Hm? What is it?"
"The word 'sentimental' is an adjective, so 'a hint of sentimental in you' makes no sense."
"Oh God! You always have to find fault with everything I say, you stupid class rep!"
After a five or so minute walk, we reach Suetsugu-chou. In other words, we've walked the distance of one station to the next.
The city streets surrounding this small station, early in the morning and late in the year, are almost completely devoid of people or sound.
"This place never changes."
"Suppose so."
It appears I wasn't the only one with that impression.
"I wonder if the store manager is still around. I'm sure the older ladies who were working part-time must've changed, at least."
Setsuna had worked at this supermarket for two years, up until the last six months of high school.
This was the place Setsuna had to give up, when she chose to walk with me by the riverside all those years ago.
"You knew I was working here the entire time, didn't you, Haruki-kun?"
"Suppose so."
I found out about her secret a whole year before I decided to talk to the braided and bespectacled girl working here.
Although admittedly… I had no idea about her nonsensical reason for keeping it all a secret.
"…You were looking at me even back then."
"Well, no, back then it wasn't more than a passing interest."
"You sure have a knack for saying stuff like that to people's faces, Haruki-kun. Blunt as ever."
With a slight pout, Setsuna quickens her pace somewhat to leave me behind.
"But in second grade you were the famous school idol, Setsuna. I never even imagined I'd ever get a chance to talk to you."
Yes, back in second grade, Setsuna was the flawless school idol.
Her fame got her wrapped up in all sorts of trouble, and even her withdrawal from the Miss Houjou High contest caused a big controversy.
Now, if you're wondering why I know about this behind-the-curtains information…
Then too bad. This is the one thing I'll take with me to the grave.
Because even if I tell her now, she'll just get unreasonably mad and say "Why didn't you tell me at the time!?" or something.
Besides, it would bring strife to Setsuna's friendship with the culprit, and that's no good.
…You better thank me, Yanagihara.
"Perhaps I'm the bigger idiot for falling in love with a man like you, Haruki-kun. I just caused myself a whole lot of pointless hardship."
"Well, uh… You can blame your own bad taste for that."
"And to think that two girls with the same bad taste would enroll in the same school. Isn't that weird?"
"…Hey!"
Lurking behind these memories of the past are recollections of events that include not just Setsuna.
"Thinking about it now, it doesn't make any sense how a guy like you could've been popular with girls.
"Stop pretending to be humble. I know that you think of yourself as equal to her, deep inside."
But now, we've come to the point where those memories don't bother us at all, whether we speak about them or keep them to ourselves.
We're long past the point of hesitating or doubting each other over things like that.
"Why of course! Even at the worst of times, I'm still the former Miss Houjou High, after all."
"But you didn't enter the contest once during university, though."
"But if I was ever in the mood to enter, I'd have probably stood a good chance at winning it."
"Do you dare say the same thing to Yanagihara?"
We've overcome many times more trials and hardships than the average couple would ever encounter.
That's why the idea of breaking up or letting our relationship fall apartーsomething we know we'd regretーis completely out of the question.
"Yup, this place hasn't changed at all either."
We walked the Houjou University grounds and the area around the main gate of the high school,
And when we finally arrived in this small park, we were able to feel the warmth of the sun.
Perhaps because this is in a residential area, or perhaps simply because it's a dull part of town, there's no one else here but us.
But to Setsuna and me, this is an unforgettable place that houses some of our deepest memories.
"This is the place you found out about my true self, Haruki-kun."
"Like I said, I already knew since a year before… Except for the fact that you were a karaoke freak."
The karaoke bar in Minami-Suetsugu that Setsuna still sometimes drags me with her to.
"Look, we were on these swings together back then."
"You should probably avoid sitting on it now. Your butt might get stuck and you might not be able to get out."
"Oh jeez! I haven't grown that much!"
In this place, Setsuna revealed her true self to me, and I could only smile with a sense of affinity at her figure.
"From that day on, I joined the Light Music Club, and a new daily life started for me."
"Thanks to a certain stubborn class rep."
"…A life unlike anything I'd ever experienced before began for me."
"…Yeah."
"Hey, Kitahara-kun."
All of a sudden, perfectly naturally, Setsuna called me how she used to call me, a long time ago…
"With this, Ogiso Setsuna's last secret has been revealed… You've just learned all about me."
A hot blaze of embarrassment ran through my body at those words, enough to turn my whole face red in an instant.
"Did you remember, perhaps?"
"Setsuna, you… Don't you feel embarrassed saying that?"
"I do! A whole bunch! I really used to like acting cute and helpless back then, now that I think back."
"Haha…"
How could I ever forget?
Those were the magic words that reminded me that the normal girl in front of me was in actuality a super idol.
From that point on, Ogiso Setsuna was to me a friend, an idol, and a very attractive girl…
I adored her, I thought she was mine, I betrayed her, I ran away from her, I lost touch with her, I tried getting closer to her, I lost touch with her again,
That lengthy history between us started with those words.
"Alright then, let's head back."
As we immersed ourselves in our typical high school lovebird chatter, the clock was already nearing eight.
We went to countless places, and we'd remind each other every time we remembered something. Treading on old ground, reflecting on old times.
Like that, we ever so slowly went about our way.
"Hey, why don't you come over for breakfast at my place? It's just around the corner from here."
"We shouldn't just barge in without telling them first."
"But mom is probably awake making lunch boxes right now, anyway."
"Is mother planning to go somewhere?"
"Yup, she's going to help us move. No doubt she plans for the whole family to come barge into our new apartment."
"Ah, haha…"
Come to think of it… I seem to remember getting a stern talking to when I said "The moving staff will do everything, so we don't need any help."
If we were to visit them now… I have no doubt they'd treat me to more onigiri, sausage, and rolled omelets than five people could ever hope to finish.
"Well, that's the kind of people they are."
"That's what it means to be family."
"That's only one embodiment of family. Not all families are like that."
"You don't like my kind of family?"
"…Back in the day, I wasn't a big fan."
Truthful words I never meant to say slip out.
Feelings so sincere, that if I were to ever utter them in front of her, she'd undoubtedly get angry with me.
But this time, I neither regret my slip of the tongue, nor make any effort to correct myself.
Because after all this time, I've learnt to believe… that after her anger and lecturing, she'll forgive me.
"Haruki-kun, you insist on lecturing others, but you can't stand getting lectured yourself, can you?"
"…I'm a twisted person. You shouldn't look up to me."
"Haruki-kun…"
But Setsuna, in response to my statement that could very well be seen as a rejection of her family, neither agrees nor disagrees, instead opting to show
Despite how twisted I am, and despite how that has caused me to commit countless sins, Setsuna meets my eyes in a completely normal manner.
"So I always wondered if it's even okay for a person like me to have a family."
"You're speaking in past tense."
"Guess so."
"What about now?"
Indeed, what about now?
Am I still the same person I was? Have I finally become a proper person?
Can I make the organization known as a "family" happy?
Not through management, training, or anything like that… but through laughing, crying, and growing up together.
"…I wonder about that. I really have no idea."
Answering that question myself wouldn't mean anything. It wouldn't lessen my insecurity any.
"Whether or not I can make everyone happy, not only you, Setsuna, but a much bigger family… I won't know that unless I try."
"…Haruki-kun."
With a peaceful smile, Setsuna looks at me.
…Even when my proud proclamation skirts around the problem, she still accepts it.
"Yeah, I won't know unless I try. So I'll have to try…"
"Yes."
Yes, let's give it a shot.
Our new apartment has two bedrooms.
There's room for one more person besides Setsuna and me.
"I want a child… A child with you, Setsuna."
"Yes."
Setsuna answered immediately.
Without a single worry about my hesitations.
"I don't know if I can be the best father, but I still want to give it a shot."
I don't know if I can be anything like Setsuna's father.
It's possible I'll just end up like my own father.
"I know you'll do just fine, Haruki-kun."
"I… pray for the same thing."
But for as long as Setsuna will continue to save me…
With Setsuna and the Ogiso family pulling me along, perhaps things will work out fine.
"Yes, yes…"
Setsuna wraps her arms around me in a tight embrace.
"I look forward to it. I'd like a boy just like you, Haruki-kun."
"Another one of me would just annoy the life out of you. I'd like a girl like you, Setsuna."
"Another one of me would just be spoiled and selfish."
"In that case… I'm fine either way."
"Yeah… either way is fine."
Early in the morning, in a deserted park, a married couple holds a somewhat embarrassing ceremony.
It was a perfectly ordinary ceremony, and perfectly natural. However, the two had promised not to do it outside.
"Well, putting that aside…"
"Hm?"
When we're done, Setsuna moves her lips to my ear, standing on her tiptoes.
"The truth is…"
And with a slight sigh, she delivers the very timely news.
It showed up positive, and when I went to the hospital, they confirmed it.
I found out yesterday…
"I had my little suspicions, but the timing felt almost too convenient, so I went to make sure at the hospital…"
I slipped away from work at noon and took an examination.
"…Were you reading my mind?"
"That goes doubly for you. It's as if you were reading my mind when you made that proclamation."
"Ha, haha…"
"Hehe…"
I tightly hug Setsuna back, making sure not to put too much pressure on her belly, of course.
"Hahaha… ahahahaha!"
I had felt so unsure for so long, but I had finally resolved myself.
But to have it all come true in a single moment feels so… strange, odd, and outlandish. Well, I guess those three things mean the same thing.
"Hey, Haruki-kun…"
But for some reason, I feel so overwhelmed with joy…
"Soon I won't be able to call you Haruki-kun anymore. I'll have to call you 'dad' when the kids are around."
Because my family in this world is once again growing bigger. Because a new resident is going to be living with us in our new apartment.
"That's why I'll use this occasion to say it to my heart's content, okay? Haruki-kun, Haruki-kun, Haruki-kun… Congratulations, and thank you so much!"
"Setsuna, Setsuna…"
Our somewhat embarrassing ceremony continues. In fact, it's only getting more embarrassing.
But I don't pay attention to any sense of embarrassment within me. None of that matters to me now.
Instead, I put all my energy into embracing the person I love.
"Setsuna…!"
The woman I will soon be calling "mom" in front of our child.
"Come on, Setsuna, don't you know we're about to leave soon? Get down here."
"Okaay! Just a minute!"
And so, at noon…
The moving truck had already taken off, and of course, the luggage was carried out by the entire family.
The only thing left was for the residents to leave as well.
"Everything's gone, huh?"
"Yeah…"
The apartment was filled with cardboard boxes just a short while ago. And up until a week prior, the apartment was full of life.
But all that remains now is the emptiness of what used to be our home.
It's a place that we're probably not going to return to again, once we go down and get in the car heading toward our new home.
It's a place that we won't be seeing ever again after seven long years of staying here.
"Let's head out, shall we?"
"Yeah…"
It's kind of pathetic to get caught up in nostalgia on the very last day, but so much has happened here…
This apartment was the background to so many events in my life. Memories that aren't limited to just Setsuna, nor to myself when I was alone.
"Let's go."
After burning the image of the empty apartment into my eyes one last time, I slowly close the door.
All that's left is to lock the door, and once this key is returned to the realtor, that'll be the end of it…
"Ah, Kitahara-san. Excuse me."
"Yes?"
"This package was meant for you, but it was delivered to my door by mistake."
"Ah, I'm sorry about that."
"Thank you very much for going out of your way to give it to us."
At the very end of our final farewell, a very kind and innocent distraction jumps in.
This time, with a slight bitter smile, I make up my mind to take my final leave…
"…Haruki-kun."
"What is it?"
When I turn around, I see Setsuna holding up a postcard right in front of my eyes.
There's a picture of what seems to be a very primiti… uh, traditional European townscape. It all but reveals the identity of the sender.
"…She says that the Vienna performance was a massive success. Apparently she's coming back this New Year's."
"Why would she send a postcard in this day and age? …She could've just sent us an email."
"Oh, but isn't this just like Kazusa? She's always been bad with technology."
"This is nothing like Kazusa! I can't believe a couch potato like her would bother sending a picture postcard!"
"Haha… You're mean, Haruki-kun."
She's the one who's being mean here.
She knows perfectly well where we live, yet she went out of her way to write the address number of the neighboring apartment door.
And she knowingly made sure it'd arrive today, to the apartment where she used to…
"…Okay, let's head out for real this time. I want to have something to eat by the end of the day, at least."
"Huh? Let's just eat outside! I'm sure my parents would allow that on a special day like this."
"Right, I suppose that's fine if you're tired, Setsuna. I guess I'll have to cook up a feast large enough for the whole family…"
"Hey! Don't embarrass me in front of my family! Haruki-kun, you're so mean!"
And so, the two of us… The two of us, soon to be the three of us…
…Will begin carving out our new history tomorrow, in a new place we'll call home…
